page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 614 GB local disk, and the instance is premium storage capable. It runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench compiling and rendering tests consistently register in the average range. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while small-block cached read performance is average at 1031.04 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% at 39.01 GB/sec and 22.73 GB/sec respectively. For language model tasks, the instance exhibits strong text generation speeds on small 135M models, though performance scales down to average levels for medium 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ads_v5 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores with a substantial local storage allocation. This configuration is well-suited for workloads such as relational databases, web serving, application servers, and moderate data processing tasks. The inclusion of 614 GB of local storage reduces the immediate need for external block storage for temporary files or caching, optimizing overall resource utilization. However, the lower uncached memory bandwidth suggests it is less optimal for memory-bound high-performance computing or massive in-memory databases.
